site.universityEn: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim's Lab, Department of Educational Technology, Ewha Womans University
overviewEn: CoRe Lab (Collaborative Research Learning Lab) is the research group of Professor Kyu Yon Lim in the Department of Educational Technology, College of Education, Ewha Womans University. Guided by our motto, “Seeing How We Learn Together,” we capture, analyze, and visualize the cognitive and social interactions that unfold among learners during collaborative learning.

The participation, emotions, and self-regulation that arise in moments of joint problem solving are rarely visible on the surface, yet they shape the quality of learning. CoRe Lab explores the question “How do we learn together?” through learning analytics and human–AI collaboration, and designs dashboards and support systems that let learners and instructors see that process for themselves.

With continuous support from the National Research Foundation of Korea in both the humanities and social sciences and in science and engineering, we study collaborative learning analytics, learning experience design (LXD), and personalized learning support systems. Our work appears in domestic and international journals, conference presentations, and patents, and our graduate students build strong records every year through conference awards and selection for national research grants.

news-mue7umbwyms.titleEn: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim’s team secures two patents for problem-solving learning support technology
news-mue7umbwyms.subtitleEn: Breaking programming problem solving into 11 steps with sequential prompts
bodyEn: A research team led by Professor Kyu Yon Lim (CoRe Lab), Department of Educational Technology, College of Education, Ewha Womans University, received decisions to grant two patents on technologies that support problem-solving learning on September 15, 2026.

The two patents are “Problem-solving learning apparatus based on prompts to aid learning and its operating method” and “Problem-solving learning apparatus based on a dashboard to aid learning and its operating method.”

The team focused on a gap left by existing learning support tools. Most tools supported only early stages such as understanding the problem or making a plan, and even those covering the whole process did not adequately support evaluation, reflection, and improvement after a solution had been produced.

Visualization tools, likewise, tended simply to display information about programming activity; few treated programming as a problem-solving process and helped learners check their own understanding, analysis, and evaluation of the problem.

The two patents fill this gap. While the prompt-based technology guides learners sequentially through the entire problem-solving process, the dashboard-based technology turns the data accumulated along the way back into information that learners can read.

The prompt-based technology divides programming problem solving into six steps of planning before coding, two steps of carrying out the coding, and three steps of reflecting after coding, and provides the cognitive and metacognitive prompts needed at each step. What learners write at one step carries over to the next, so the flow from planning to execution to reflection is built into the interface.
[사진2]

The dashboard-based technology visualizes, as a graph, the achievement level learners rate for themselves after each step, and adds explanations grouped into strengths and areas for improvement. Experts’ actual behavior distributions and the frequency of each type of error learners encountered are also presented, so learners can examine their problem-solving process from several angles.
[사진3]

The inventors are Professor Kyu Yon Lim, Dr. Hyejun Kim, Juwon Lee (Ph.D. candidate), Eunju Park (M.A.), and Haeun Park (M.A.). Both patents result from the mid-career research project “Designing an AI-based Personalized Learning Model and Online Platform for SW Education,” supported for three years from 2020 by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Research Foundation of Korea under the Basic Research Program in Science and Engineering.

2026-09-sample-news.titleEn: Ph.D. student Juwon Lee selected for the NRF Doctoral Student Research Grant
bodyEn: Juwon Lee, a Ph.D. student in the Department of Educational Technology, College of Education, Ewha Womans University (advisor: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim), has been selected for the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) 2026 Doctoral Student Research Grant in the Humanities and Social Sciences.

The program, run by the NRF to support stable research activity and strengthen the research capacity of doctoral students in the humanities and social sciences, provides KRW 20 million per year for two years. With a selection rate of about 31% for new projects (as of 2026), it is regarded as one of the most competitive national research grants for doctoral students.

After earning her master’s degree in Educational Technology at Ewha in 2023, Lee continued into the doctoral program. As principal investigator, she will receive two years of funding to conduct research on “Developing and Validating an AI-based System to Support Collaborative Knowledge Building.”

news-jyj-award-2026.titleEn: Dr. Yujin Jung receives Ewha Graduate School Outstanding Dissertation Award (Spring 2026)
news-jyj-award-2026.subtitleEn: Exploring teachers’ roles in the age of generative AI through actor-network theory
bodyEn: Dr. Yujin Jung (advisor: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim), who earned her bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees in Educational Technology at Ewha, received the Ewha Womans University Graduate School Outstanding Dissertation Award for the spring semester of 2026. The award-winning work is her doctoral dissertation, “Exploring the Network Formation of Teachers and Generative AI and Teachers’ Roles in Instructional Contexts: Focusing on Actor-Network Theory.”

As generative AI is rapidly introduced into schools, the study explored how interactions between teachers and generative AI vary across instructional contexts and how teachers’ roles take shape in the process. Dr. Jung viewed generative AI as an actor that influences teachers’ practice and adopted actor-network theory as her analytic framework.

The analysis showed that teachers did not simply produce materials themselves. They made appropriate requests to generative AI, reviewed and selected its outputs, and decided where AI would sit in the lesson and how it would be used. When students used generative AI, teachers observed those interactions and intervened or facilitated as needed. On this basis, Dr. Jung interpreted teachers’ roles not as fixed, but as formed and transformed through interaction with generative AI.

In an interview with the Ewha graduate school newspaper, Dr. Jung advised students preparing their theses to “just start writing.” “Even a problem that won’t come together in your head starts to show where the logic is missing and what needs more thought once you put it into writing,” she said.

Dr. Jung plans to continue studying interactions between humans and generative AI in teaching and learning contexts, examining how instructors and learners interact with generative AI to identify factors that shape educationally meaningful interactions and the support they need.
The interview appeared in the “Academic News” section of Ewha Graduate School Newspaper No. 107.

news-munfl7f6252.titleEn: Dr. Hyejun Kim receives Ewha Graduate School Outstanding Dissertation Award (Fall 2024)
news-munfl7f6252.subtitleEn: What happens when learners choose their own scaffolding?
bodyEn: Dr. Hyejun Kim (advisor: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim), who earned her bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees in Educational Technology at Ewha, received the Outstanding Dissertation Award from the Ewha Womans University Graduate School for the fall semester of 2024.

Her dissertation, “Exploring College Learners’ Problem-Solving Performance and Scaffolding Use Behaviors in Programming Problem Solving: Focusing on Shared Control,” began from the concern that over-reliance on AI tools can weaken learner agency. Dr. Kim proposed “scaffolding control” as a way to support problem solving without learners losing ownership, extending the established notion of learner control over sequence, pace, and feedback to scaffolding itself.

To examine this, she developed mySTEPS, a scaffolding tool for programming problem solving. mySTEPS provides 24 scaffolds across 11 steps, from problem representation to solution design, execution and evaluation, and reflection. The system preselects scaffolds based on problem difficulty, and learners can accept or reject them, add others, and change their choices during problem solving—implementing “shared control” in which the system and the learner divide control.

Eleven college students solved two programming problems of different difficulty, and Dr. Kim analyzed their behavior by triangulating screen recordings, think-aloud protocols, and interviews. Learners judged whether a scaffold was necessary and useful, and chose scaffolds by considering their own characteristics, the difficulty of the problem, and how the solution was actually unfolding. Even scaffolds chosen beforehand were skipped if they seemed unnecessary mid-task, and added when they became necessary. This decision process looked similar across problem difficulty and solution scores.

The study offers a theoretical basis for extending the object of control to scaffolding. It also proposes concrete design guidance: let learners control scaffolds whose necessity depends on learner characteristics (such as checking requirements) before problem solving, and scaffolds whose necessity depends on the solution process (such as comparing code) during problem solving.

news-munfhmipt8m.titleEn: Dr. Myunghwa Jin receives the KSET Outstanding Doctoral Dissertation Award
news-munfhmipt8m.subtitleEn: Real-time adaptive feedback deepens cognitive engagement in collaborative learning
bodyEn: Dr. Myunghwa Jin (advisor: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim), who earned her master’s and doctoral degrees in Educational Technology at Ewha, received the Outstanding Doctoral Dissertation Award at the 2025 Spring Conference of the Korean Society for Educational Technology (KSET). The society selects and honors outstanding doctoral dissertations.

Her dissertation, “The Effects of Real-time Adaptive Feedback on Cognitive Engagement and Interaction in Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL),” started from the observation that collaborative learning moves quickly, making it hard for learners to reflect on their own, so instructional support must also be delivered in real time.

Dr. Jin designed SCoLA (Supporting Collaborative Learning with Adaptive feedback), an adaptive collaborative learning support tool. SCoLA analyzes learners’ chat messages in real time in terms of cognitive engagement and interaction, and provides feedback. The analysis was automated using generative-AI text classification and social network analysis, and the feedback combined descriptive feedback on the current state with prescriptive feedback guiding improvement.

Forty-eight pre-service teachers were divided into 12 teams, with six teams each in experimental and control groups. The experimental group, which received real-time adaptive feedback, showed deeper cognitive engagement, such as integrating ideas, and higher network density—meaning messages connected to one another rather than breaking off. These differences did not appear early in the collaboration but emerged significantly in the middle and later phases.

The study provides a theoretical foundation for designing real-time adaptive feedback that supports synchronous collaborative learning, and empirically shows the importance of examining collaboration over time and of supporting both its cognitive and social dimensions.

news-mumwtjuuqkl.titleEn: Dr. Jiyoung Lim appointed faculty member at Busan National University of Education
bodyEn: Dr. Jiyoung Lim (advisor: Prof. Kyu Yon Lim), who earned her doctorate in Educational Technology at Ewha, was appointed as a full-time faculty member at Busan National University of Education in September 2025.

Dr. Lim completed her bachelor’s degree and a master’s in psychology (psychometrics) in Ewha’s Department of Psychology before moving to educational technology for her doctorate. Her path—beginning in psychology and broadening into educational technology—has now come to fruition with this appointment.

Dr. Lim has also built a strong research record. As principal investigator, she has secured an NRF Early-Career Research Grant in Science and Engineering (2023–2025) and an NRF Collaborative Research Grant in the Humanities and Social Sciences (2025–2028). She received Ewha’s Excellence in Teaching Award (2020) and the KSET Outstanding Paper Award (2022, 2026). Her current research focuses on technology-based learning design, digital literacy education, and AI- and digital-enhanced education.

lim-gyuyeon.affiliationEn: Department of Educational Technology, Ewha Womans University
lim-gyuyeon.bioEn: Kyu Yon Lim is a Professor in the Department of Educational Technology, College of Education, Ewha Womans University, where she conducts research on technology-enhanced learning, collaborative and self-regulated learning, and learning experience design (LXD). She has led or co-led a range of research projects, including NRF early-career, mid-career, and convergence research grants in the humanities and social sciences and BK21 Plus projects, and has received mid-career grants in science and engineering for designing dashboards for online learning (2017–2019) and designing personalized learning (2020–2022). She is currently the principal investigator of projects on teacher–AI collaboration (2024–2026) and collaborative learning analytics (2023–2025). She received Ewha’s Excellence in Teaching Award in 2014 and the Graduate School of Education Excellence in Teaching Award in 2022.

lablife-mufb1ayuga0.captionEn: Wrapping Up Our Science & Engineering Project, 2023
lablife-mufb1ayuga0.bodyEn: Wrapping up three years of NRF science and engineering research that began in 2020—a commemorative photo with the research team on February 23, 2023!! Thank you all for your hard work~~

lablife-mufhc35fwhd.captionEn: One Spring Day in 2026.. The Day We Resolved to Join CoRe Lab
lablife-mufhc35fwhd.bodyEn: At CoRe Lab lives the ‘Lim fan club’... fangirling in progress...

lablife-muiepdx5kjx.bodyEn:
Dahye Lee (M.A.) and Dr. Myunghwa Jin, who graduated in spring 2024, and Dr. Hyejun Kim, who graduated in fall 2024, started a CoRe Lab tradition:
a commemorative photo in front of the professor’s office! Ta-da~🥁!!

To the three who studied so hard and graduated with wonderful theses—
we wish you nothing but bright paths ahead :)
- All of CoRe Lab.

lablife-muieubwl8ke.bodyEn: At the Korean Society for Educational Technology Spring Conference on May 31, 2025, CoRe Lab’s pride, Dr. Myunghwa Jin, received the Outstanding Doctoral Dissertation Award. 🥳💐

lablife-munt1vvfbp9.bodyEn:
The day the first snow (a blizzard!) fell while Juram & Hyojeong were studying together at the Industry–Academia Cooperation Building.
A romantic shot with an international student we met for the first time while escaping the snowy path☃️🤳🏻

We’re also attaching scenes of the campus full of romance on the day of the first snow~

lablife-mv26q7je1gz.bodyEn:
I lift my head and gaze at the night sky
I see a single star shining far away
Ah, when will I ever reach that place?
With that star as my guide, I walk this path
That star is... the North Star, ‘LIM’
